name: DMR digital voice
label: DMR
notes: DMR digital voice (4FSK, 4800 baud, AMBE+2) on any 12500 Hz channel, a repeater's two time slots or a handheld's bursts; start it on the measured centre. Each call gives two events, one when its link control is in hand (at its header, or within a superframe when the job joins mid-call) and one at its end (`eot`), naming the calling radio (`src`), the talkgroup or called radio (`dst`), the call type, the colour code (`color_code`), the slot (`slot`, null for a handheld) and `origin`; an idle or control-only repeater gives one `type: channel` event instead. Both slots are decoded at once and the job has two voices, `slot1` and `slot2` (a handheld's speech is on `slot1`): attach transcribe to one with `stream`. Its main audio stream, what play, the mix and a plain attach hear, follows the job's `audio_policy`: `first_active` (the default) the call that started first, until it ends; `follow` that call, then the one still going when it ends; `all` both mixed. Each call event's `stream` names its slot's voice and `program` says whether it is on the main stream. The speech needs zeta-mbe, which the operator builds with `bash tools/install-vocoders.sh` from a source checkout; without it the calls are still reported with `audio: false` and `silent: no_vocoder`, and `job_context.dmr.vocoder` says how to install it. Encrypted calls are reported (`silent: encrypted`), never decoded.
